brief: US equities rallied sharply, with the S&P up 2.3% and the Nasdaq up 3.4%, the broadest advance in nearly a year and the biggest single day in over seven months, as all 11 sectors gained. Asia followed higher, led by Korea's KOSPI (+5%) and SoftBank (about +15% ahead of earnings), while Taiwan's October exports hit a record, beating estimates. Crude fell to its lowest level since August (Brent $91.7, WTI $86.2) after President Trump said Iran is militarily effectively over, unwinding the oil war-risk premium. CTA systematic equity exposure turned negative (-5%). With real money not selling and corporate buybacks resuming next week, the note argues the feedback loop that amplifies headline-driven selling has largely been removed, leaving cross-asset volatility muted ahead of the afternoon's US CPI print (consensus 0.3% month on month). UBS's European equity derivatives desk had a very active day: asset managers added over $1.5bn to European major longs, buying Euro Banks and Travel and Leisure, with the only sell flow being partial profit taking in OMX.
